candidate_falsified: an arbitrary nonlocal positive kernel can replace the signed diagonal Weil kernel while agreeing with its quadratic form on a full linear test space
polarization: a complex quadratic form Q determines its sesquilinear form B uniquely by B(f,g)=1/4 sum_(k=0)^3 i^k Q(f+i^k g)
kernel_consequence: if two continuous kernels agree on Q(f) for every f in a linear form core, they agree on all cross pairings and hence define the same distributional kernel on that core
signed_diagonal: on a faithful full test space, the local Weil form has kernel W(u) delta(u-v); a different positive nonlocal kernel cannot reproduce it if this diagonal form has a negative direction
compression_escape: for a restricted feature map B, the compressed form B* D B may be positive although D is indefinite; this requires a named non-surjective image or quotient and positivity must be proved there
conclusion: nonlocality alone is not a positivity mechanism; the surviving object is an explicit restricted feature map plus a positive compression identity
acceptance_test: Name a non-surjective source feature map B_t whose image is exactly the admissible heat-polynomial form domain, compute B_t* W_t B_t before GNS, and prove its positivity by an identity not implied by the target cone.
